summary: Conor Roddy is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2011) under Kathleen Marie Higgins. He also studied under William Lyons, Arindam Chakrabarti, Graham Parkes, and Roger T. Ames.

Conrad Bursian (1830–1883) was a scholar of archaeology and history educated at Leipzig and Berlin. He held posts at the universities of Leipzig (~1856–1861), Zurich (~1861–1864), Tübingen (~1864–1869), Jena (~1869–1874), and Munich (~1874–1883).
Conrad M. Arensberg (1910–1997) studied at Harvard University (~1927–1934) and held an academic post at Columbia University from around 1946 to 1979.

Constance E. Kassor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Smith College and Emory University (PhD attested 2014) under John D. Dunne and Sara L. McClintock, later serving on the faculty at Smith College (attested 2014).
Constance Powell Chin is a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. She studied under Christian Luczanits and completed a master's degree at San Jose State University by 2012.

Constantin Régamey (1907–1982) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and linguist. Educated at the universities of Warsaw and Paris, he taught at Warsaw (1936), Fribourg (1945), and Lausanne (1945; 1949–1957), and presided over the Swiss Society for Asian Studies (1962–1971).
Corneille Jest (1930–2019) was a Tibetologist and archaeologist educated at Paris Descartes University who studied under André Leroi-Gourhan in 1972. He held a post at the CNRS.

Cornelis Jan Kuiken is a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Groningen by 2002, supervised by Timothy Hugh Barrett and Jan N. Bremmer, having also studied under Jaap den Hollander.

Cornelis Petrus Tiele (1830–1902) was a religious studies and Iranian scholar. Educated in Amsterdam, he served at the Remonstrant Seminary (1873), held a professorship at Leiden University (1877–1901), and was Gifford Lecturer at the University of Edinburgh (1896).
Corrado Pensa is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Giuseppe Tucci and Raniero Gnoli. He served as a professor at the University of Rome (attested 1971).
Craig J. Reynolds is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1996 and 2016).

Craig Jamieson is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Cambridge as curator for the South Asia manuscript collection (attested 2002, 2012) and at Queens' College, Cambridge, as a fellow (attested 2012).
Craig Preston is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Virginia under Joe Bransford Wilson and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Cristina Pecchia is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. She completed a PhD at the University of Rome (~1998–2003) and also studied at the University of Vienna, later holding posts at Vienna and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~2008).

Cristina Scherrer-Schaub (born 1947) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. She studied under Bocheński, Geiger, Levinas, and Segre, later holding professorships at the University of Lausanne (~1998–2012) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2000–2015).

Csaba Dezső (born 1973) is an Indologist who earned his master's degrees from Eötvös Loránd University and his PhD (1998–2004) from the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. He became an assistant lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University around 2002.

Csaba Kiss is an Indologist who earned his D.Phil. at the University of Oxford (2003–2009) under Alexis Sanderson. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University, the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021), and Studies on the History of Śaivism (attested 2021).

Cuilan Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and sinology. She held an assistant professorship at Emmanuel College, Toronto (attested 2017) and a post at the University of Munich (attested 2018).
Culadasa (1944–2021) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure who studied under Joti Dhamma Bhikkhu and served as director of the Dharma Treasure Buddhist Sangha (attested 2011).
Cuma Ozkan is a scholar of religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at the University of Iowa under the supervision of Morten Schlütter (attested 2013).
